boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Oakland University
boards.description: Current, under-21-safe food stops around Oakland University with official location pages that document evening availability.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Crooks Road
cards.subtitle: 2290 Crooks Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need food after campus dining hours; the official location page lists service until 4 AM every day.
cards.short_summary: A nearby drive-thru option with the latest verified hours in this set.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell at 2290 Crooks Road lists drive-thru hours of 7 AM–4 AM daily and dine-in hours through midnight.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed daily until 4 AM; dine-in is listed until 12 AM. Check the location page for holiday changes.

cards.entity_name: Chipotle Mexican Grill — 84 N Adams Road
cards.title: Chipotle on North Adams
cards.subtitle: 84 N Adams Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Plan pickup before the 11 PM close; the location page confirms both the address and daily store hours for this Rochester Hills site.
cards.short_summary: A documented 11 PM pickup stop on North Adams Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Chipotle’s 84 N Adams Road location lists store hours of 10:45 AM–11 PM Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed daily hours run to 11 PM; in-store pickup and delivery are identified on the official page.

cards.title: Wendy's on South Rochester Road
cards.subtitle: 3140 S Rochester Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Choose dine-in or drive-thru for a later meal; this location’s official page lists both options open until 1 AM daily.
cards.short_summary: A Rochester Road restaurant with verified 1 AM service.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s at 3140 S Rochester Road lists restaurant and drive-thru hours of 9 AM–1 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru are both listed until 1 AM daily; the operator notes that holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Hamlin To-Go
cards.subtitle: 1484 N Rochester Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Order for pickup when an evening meal is needed; the official To-Go page lists weekday hours through 11 PM and its location details.
cards.short_summary: A takeout-focused option with an official 11 PM weekday closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamlin Pub To-Go at 1484 N Rochester Road lists hours of 10 AM–11 PM Monday–Friday and 10 AM–10 PM Saturday–Sunday.
cards.access_notes: The official page identifies this as a pickup location; weekdays are listed until 11 PM and weekends until 10 PM.

cards.title: RH House
cards.subtitle: 2630 Crooks Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Check the day before heading over: RH House lists Friday and Saturday service until 11 PM, with earlier closing on other nights.
cards.short_summary: A Crooks Road restaurant with verified 11 PM weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: RH House lists hours until 11 PM on Friday and Saturday, 10 PM Monday–Thursday, and 9 PM Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Friday and Saturday are listed until 11 PM. Confirm the day’s service before leaving campus.

cards.title: Shish Palace on Livernois
cards.subtitle: 165 S Livernois Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Keep this Livernois location in mind for an evening meal; the restaurant’s official site lists the Rochester Hills dining room until 10 PM daily.
cards.short_summary: A Mediterranean-food stop with daily 10 PM hours posted by the restaurant.
cards.evidence_claim: Shish Palace lists its Rochester Hills location at 165 S Livernois Road as open 10 AM–10 PM all week.
cards.access_notes: The official location listing states 10 AM–10 PM all week for Rochester Hills.

cards.title: Miyako Japanese Steakhouse
cards.subtitle: 173 S Livernois Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Aim for Friday or Saturday for the latest listed service; Miyako posts 10:30 PM closing on those nights at its Livernois location.
cards.short_summary: A Japanese steakhouse with official 10:30 PM Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Miyako Japanese Steakhouse lists Friday and Saturday hours through 10:30 PM at 173 S Livernois Road.
cards.access_notes: Friday service is listed 4:30–10:30 PM and Saturday noon–10:30 PM; other days close earlier.

cards.title: Lino's North
cards.subtitle: 4856 Adams Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: For a later dinner window, go Friday or Saturday: Lino’s North lists 4–10 PM service on both nights at its Adams Road address.
cards.short_summary: An Adams Road Italian restaurant with verified 10 PM Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Lino’s North lists Friday and Saturday hours of 4–10 PM at 4856 Adams Road in Rochester Hills.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists Friday and Saturday through 10 PM; Monday–Thursday and Sunday close earlier.

cards.title: Ram's Horn on Rochester Road
cards.subtitle: 1990 S Rochester Road, Rochester Hills
cards.notes: Use the Friday or Saturday closing window for a later diner meal; the restaurant posts service until 10 PM on those two nights.
cards.short_summary: A family-operated diner with official 10 PM Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Ram’s Horn Rochester Hills lists everyday hours of 7 AM–9 PM, with Friday and Saturday open until 10 PM.
cards.access_notes: Friday and Saturday are listed until 10 PM; all hours are stated as subject to change.

cards.title: Buddy's Pizza in Auburn Hills
cards.subtitle: 2612 N Squirrel Road, Auburn Hills
cards.notes: Use the Friday or Saturday 11 PM window for pizza; Buddy’s official location page lists its Auburn Hills restaurant hours and ordering options.
cards.short_summary: A nearby pizza restaurant with verified 11 PM Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Buddy’s Pizza Auburn Hills lists Friday and Saturday hours of 11 AM–11 PM at 2612 N Squirrel Road.
cards.access_notes: Friday and Saturday hours are listed through 11 PM; weekday hours end at 10 PM and Sunday at 9 PM.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified no-cost activities at Oakland University, including options open to students and several open to the public.

cards.title: Play games at the Grizz Den
cards.subtitle: Oakland Center, Oakland University
cards.notes: Bring friends to the Oakland Center for console games, billiards, foosball, board games, card games, air hockey, or PC stations.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost campus game room for the OU community.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University states that the Grizz Den is free for OU students, faculty, staff, and alumni, with consoles, games, billiards, PCs, and other activities.
cards.access_notes: Free for OU students, faculty, staff, and alumni; located in the Oakland Center.

cards.title: Settle in at Kresge Library
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library, Oakland University
cards.notes: Meet up to read, research, or use a library workstation; visitors may request computer access with photo identification at a service desk.
cards.short_summary: A library hang with guest access to most online resources on site.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries says visitors are welcome in Kresge Library, may access most online resources from its workstations, and can obtain guest computer authorization with photo ID.
cards.access_notes: Visitors are welcome; check current library hours before going. Guest computer authorization requires a current photo ID.

cards.title: Catch an OU Art Gallery program
cards.subtitle: Oakland University Art Gallery, West Wilson Hall
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current programming, then meet at West Wilson Hall for an exhibition-related talk, panel, or other public event.
cards.short_summary: Free, public-facing visual-art programming on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University states that all Oakland University Art Gallery events are free and open to all.
cards.source_title: OU Art Gallery Exhibition — Oakland University
cards.access_notes: Gallery programming and seasonal hours vary; confirm the current event listing before visiting.

cards.title: Hear the Elliott Tower carillon
cards.subtitle: Elliott Tower, Oakland University
cards.notes: Plan a daytime meet-up around a Friday noon performance, or watch for the outdoor Six Fridays at 6 summer concert series.
cards.short_summary: Live carillon music at a prominent campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University says Elliott Tower has live performances every Friday at noon and that its Six Fridays at 6 outdoor carillon concerts are free.
cards.access_notes: Friday-noon performances and the summer series are subject to the university’s current schedule and weather conditions.

cards.title: Try the Priority Health Fitness Court
cards.subtitle: Recreation Center area, Oakland University
cards.notes: Use the open-air bodyweight circuit with a friend, or follow a short workout through the free Fitness Court mobile app.
cards.short_summary: A public outdoor circuit-training stop for a quick movement break.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University describes the Priority Health Fitness Court as a free outdoor circuit-training facility available to the public and suitable for ages 14 and up.
cards.source_title: Fitness Court — University Recreation and Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Available to the public; the university identifies it as appropriate for ages 14+ and all fitness levels.

cards.title: Walk the indoor track
cards.subtitle: Recreation Center, Oakland University
cards.notes: Use the four-lane indoor track for an easy walk-and-talk session; bring your GrizzCard if you are an enrolled OU student.
cards.short_summary: An indoor stroll option included with eligible student access.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recreation Center lists a four-lane indoor track, and Oakland University says registered students have free access to the Recreation Center.
cards.source_title: Recreation Center — University Recreation and Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Free for enrolled OU students through Rec Center access; nonmembers need a membership, day pass, or swim pass.

cards.title: Shoot around in the 3-Court Gym
cards.subtitle: Recreation Center, Oakland University
cards.notes: Coordinate a casual basketball session during open recreation and check out a basketball at no fee with a valid Rec Center membership card.
cards.short_summary: A low-key court hang with no-fee ball checkout for members.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recreation Center lists basketball open recreation in its 3-Court Gym and basketballs among its no-fee equipment checkouts.
cards.source_title: Recreation Center — University Recreation and Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Requires valid Rec Center membership access; confirm open-recreation availability before arriving.

cards.title: Play racquetball at the Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Recreation Center, Oakland University
cards.notes: Reserve or use a racquetball court during available recreation time; members can check out racquetball rackets without a fee.
cards.short_summary: An included indoor activity with no-fee racket checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recreation Center lists two racquetball courts and racquetball rackets among equipment available for no-fee checkout.
cards.source_title: Recreation Center — University Recreation and Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Requires valid Rec Center membership access; check facility scheduling and court availability in advance.

cards.title: Join a Group X class
cards.subtitle: University Recreation and Well-Being, Oakland University
cards.notes: Choose a Group X workout from the current schedule and register online or at arrival; available spots are first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: Instructor-led fitness and social time included for OU students.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University says all scheduled Group Exercise classes are free for students, faculty, staff, and Recreation Center members.
cards.source_title: Group Exercise — University Recreation and Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Free for OU students, faculty, staff, and Rec Center members; preregistration is encouraged and spaces are first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Plan a pool session
cards.subtitle: Recreation Center Aquatic Center, Oakland University
cards.notes: Use the Aquatic Center as part of eligible student Rec Center access, and review the current facility schedule before meeting at the pool.
cards.short_summary: A campus swim option included in student Rec Center membership.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University states that student Rec Center memberships are included in tuition with at least one paid credit hour and that memberships include the Aquatic Center.
cards.access_notes: Free to eligible OU students through membership included in tuition; nonmembers must purchase a membership, day pass, or swim pass.

warnings: Several Rec Center activities are free for eligible Oakland University students through access included in tuition; visitors and community members may face membership or pass charges. Confirm facility schedules before visiting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Documented Oakland University study settings, including quiet library floors, collaborative work areas, and campus common spaces.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library · second floor
cards.notes: Set up here for desktop access, printing, or shared project work. Use the second-floor service desk when you need library or technology help.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor library workspace with computers, study areas, and collaboration-oriented seating.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries identifies Kresge Library's second floor as its main floor with computers, cabanas, study rooms, and collaboration areas.
cards.access_notes: Inside Kresge Library; consult the library's current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Kresge Library Cabanas
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library · second floor
cards.notes: Use a cabana when your group needs a shared screen for a working session. Keep the conversation focused and leave the setup ready for the next users.
cards.short_summary: Second-floor group-study seating with large-screen computer collaboration tools.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries lists cabanas with wall-mounted computers on Kresge Library's second floor and recommends that floor for group study.
cards.access_notes: Located on Kresge Library's second floor; availability is not reservable through the cited page.

cards.title: Media Collaboration Rooms
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library · second floor
cards.notes: Choose a media collaboration room for a project that benefits from a large shared display. Confirm room availability and any booking requirements before arrival.
cards.short_summary: A library option for groups working with shared-screen media and project materials.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries lists media collaboration rooms among the second-floor group-study options at Kresge Library.
cards.access_notes: Located in Kresge Library; check the library's current space and reservation information.

cards.title: Kresge Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library · quiet study floor
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from a quieter setting. Avoid calls and large group meetings, as the floor is designated for quiet study.
cards.short_summary: The library's quiet-study floor, with individual tables and study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries states that Kresge Library's third floor is the quiet study floor and lists individual study tables and study rooms there.
cards.access_notes: Inside Kresge Library; follow the floor's quiet-study guidance and check building hours.

cards.title: Kresge Library Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library · group-study floor
cards.notes: Meet here when your work needs conversation and shared materials. The floor has group tables, study rooms, and a media collaboration alcove.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor library setting designed around group study and collaborative seating.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries identifies Kresge Library's fourth floor as ideal for group study and lists group tables, a media collaboration alcove, and study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Inside Kresge Library; fourth-floor study rooms are first come, first served according to OU Libraries.

cards.title: Reflection Room 426
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library · fourth floor
cards.notes: Use this named room for a brief reset between study blocks, then return to your work with a clear plan for the next task.
cards.short_summary: A named reflection room on Kresge Library's fourth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries lists a reflection room, Room 426, on the fourth floor of Kresge Library.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Kresge Library; observe room guidance and check the library's current building hours.

cards.title: Medical Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Kresge Library · first floor
cards.notes: Use an individual room for focused work if you qualify for the space. The listed medical-library study rooms operate while the Kresge building is open.
cards.short_summary: First-floor individual and group study rooms associated with Oakland University's Medical Library.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Libraries states that Medical Library study rooms on Kresge Library's first floor are open whenever the Kresge Library building is open, with individual rooms first come, first served.
cards.access_notes: Medical Library study rooms are listed as open when Kresge Library is open; individual rooms are first come, first served.

cards.title: Engineering Center Atrium
cards.subtitle: Engineering Center · campus common area
cards.notes: Use the atrium's common-area setting for a study block between engineering classes. Bring your own device and select a seat that suits the work you need to do.
cards.short_summary: A named campus common area identified by Student Involvement as a study location.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University's Office for Student Involvement lists the Engineering Center atrium and other common areas among campus study spots.
cards.source_title: Commuter Connection | Office for Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: A common area rather than a reservable room; building access conditions may vary.

cards.title: Human Health Building Common Areas
cards.subtitle: Human Health Building · floors 2–4
cards.notes: Settle into a couch or other comfortable seating on floors two through four for independent work. Keep your materials compact in this shared common area.
cards.short_summary: Common-area seating on three floors of the Human Health Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University's Office for Student Involvement lists Human Health Building common areas with couches and comfortable seating on the second, third, and fourth floors as study spots.
cards.source_title: Commuter Connection | Office for Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: Shared common areas; building access conditions and available seating may vary.

cards.title: Student Technology Center
cards.subtitle: Oakland Center · campus student center
cards.notes: Use this campus technology location when your assignment requires a workstation or technical help. Check the center's current services before planning a long session.
cards.short_summary: A named Oakland Center technology resource listed among campus study locations.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University's Office for Student Involvement lists the Student Technology Center in the Oakland Center among campus study spots.
cards.source_title: Commuter Connection | Office for Student Involvement
cards.access_notes: Located in the Oakland Center; consult the center for current hours, access, and available technology.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Oakland University rituals, recurring events, and ceremonial customs—with historical items clearly labeled.

cards.title: Celebrate the founder's birthday
cards.subtitle: Annual October campus celebration
cards.notes: Look for the October Birthday Bash honoring founder Matilda Dodge Wilson; use the event as a prompt to explore the university’s Meadow Brook roots.
cards.short_summary: Oakland’s founder is still celebrated with an annual campus birthday event.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University’s alumni publication says the annual Matilda’s Birthday Bash continues as a campus event highlight.
cards.source_title: Then and Now: The OUAA’s 50-Year Journey
cards.access_notes: Check Oakland University’s event listings for the current year’s program and attendance details.

cards.title: Dress up for Meadow Brook Ball
cards.subtitle: Meadow Brook Hall student tradition since 1974
cards.notes: Watch for committee announcements and, if attending, plan around the formal evening at Meadow Brook Hall with food, dancing, and entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A student-organized formal at Meadow Brook Hall that dates to 1974.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University’s Student Involvement directory identifies Meadow Brook Ball as one of OU’s oldest traditions and says its committee has hosted it since 1974.
cards.access_notes: Event participation and ticketing details vary by year; consult the Meadow Brook Ball Committee’s current announcements.

cards.entity_name: The Rock near the Oakland Center
cards.title: Add your mark to the Rock
cards.subtitle: Near the Oakland Center
cards.notes: See the painted Rock near the student center and follow current university guidance before participating; its changing layers preserve a long-running student practice.
cards.short_summary: Painting the Rock is recorded among Oakland student traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University’s alumni publication lists painting the rock near the student center among remembered OU traditions.
cards.source_title: Then and Now: The OUAA’s 50-Year Journey
cards.access_notes: Confirm any current painting rules or event permissions with Oakland University before adding paint.

cards.entity_name: Midnight Walk to Meadow Brook Hall
cards.title: Remember the Midnight Walk
cards.subtitle: Historic first-year orientation tradition
cards.notes: Treat this as a documented historical orientation tradition: the walk paired new students with alumni-led stories and legends around Meadow Brook Hall.
cards.short_summary: A historic overnight-orientation walk introduced newcomers to campus legends.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University documented the Midnight Walk as a distinctly OU tradition during first-year orientation, including a Legends, Myths, and Tales Tour.
cards.source_title: OU legends abound at Midnight Walk to Meadow Brook Hall
cards.access_notes: Historical item: the source documents a 2013 orientation activity; do not assume it is currently offered.

cards.title: Climb Elliott Tower as a senior
cards.subtitle: Elliott Tower graduation ritual
cards.notes: If you are an eligible graduating student, follow the university’s current instructions for the Senior Climb, commemorative photo, and tower-signing tradition.
cards.short_summary: Graduates climb Elliott Tower, photograph the moment, and sign their names.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University reports that graduates take part in the Senior Climb by climbing Elliott Tower’s steps, taking a commemorative photo, and signing their names.
cards.access_notes: Eligibility and scheduling are event-specific; verify current Senior Climb details with Oakland University.

cards.title: Join the Golden Grizzly Clap-In
cards.subtitle: Elliott Tower to the O’rena
cards.notes: At New Student Welcome, faculty, staff, and student leaders line the route from Elliott Tower to the O’rena to clap in incoming Grizzlies.
cards.short_summary: New students enter their official welcome through a campus Clap-In.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University describes New Student Welcome as a long-standing tradition and identifies its Clap-In route from Elliott Tower to the O’rena.
cards.source_title: Volunteers sought for New Student Welcome event
cards.access_notes: This is tied to the fall New Student Welcome; check the current orientation schedule for participation details.

cards.title: Make a film in 24 hours
cards.subtitle: Film and Theatre programs
cards.notes: Form a team for the annual challenge, then shoot and edit a short film within 24 hours using your own gear or designated program resources.
cards.short_summary: OU teams create short films on a one-day production clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University calls the 24-Hour Film Challenge an important annual tradition of its Film and Theatre programs.
cards.source_title: Oakland University hosts 11th annual 24-Hour Film Challenge
cards.access_notes: The 2025 event used Varner Hall editing lab 228; confirm current challenge dates, equipment access, and submission rules.

cards.title: Mark Hispanic Heritage Month at OU
cards.subtitle: September 15–October 15 campus observance
cards.notes: Follow the Center for Multicultural Initiatives’ annual program of talks and events recognizing Hispanic histories, politics, culture, and contributions.
cards.short_summary: OU maintains a long-standing campus observance of Hispanic Heritage Month.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University states that recognizing National Hispanic Heritage Month is a long-standing OU tradition.
cards.source_title: Oakland University celebrates National Hispanic Heritage Month
cards.access_notes: Programming changes annually; consult the Center for Multicultural Initiatives’ current event schedule.

cards.title: Spot the oak-and-obsidian mace
cards.subtitle: Commencement and convocation ceremonial processional
cards.notes: At a university ceremony, look for the marshal carrying OU’s scepter mace; it signals the arrival of the faculty processional.
cards.short_summary: OU’s distinctive mace leads major academic ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University says its mace, created in 1994, is carried at commencement, convocation, and other ceremonies to signify the faculty processional’s arrival.
cards.access_notes: Observe this ceremonial tradition during a public commencement or convocation; access follows the particular event’s attendance policies.

cards.title: Attend the President’s Colloquium
cards.subtitle: Annual faculty scholarship lecture series
cards.notes: Watch for the annual colloquium and attend a faculty presentation that connects scholarly work with broad questions across science, history, politics, or humanities.
cards.short_summary: A yearly lecture tradition showcasing Oakland faculty scholarship.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University states that the President’s Colloquium began in 1995 and is an annual Oakland tradition centered on faculty academic and research work.
cards.access_notes: The source documents the annual series; verify the current year’s speaker, venue, and public attendance information.

warnings: The Midnight Walk is explicitly labeled historical because the direct source documents its 2013 orientation use rather than a current offering.
The President’s Colloquium source documents the annual tradition but predates the template freshness window; current scheduling should be confirmed.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Oakland University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that moves from campus orientation and food to recreation, arts, and a historic campus landmark.

cards.title: Start at the Oakland Center
cards.subtitle: Find the campus gathering place
cards.notes: Begin by walking through the Oakland Center to locate meeting spaces, student-organization offices, campus services, and the food court for later.
cards.short_summary: Use the main student center as a practical first reference point.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland Center hosts conferences and events, student organization offices and meeting spaces, Pioneer Food Court, credit union, and Gear Shop.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists building hours; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Pick a lunch option at Pioneer Food Court
cards.subtitle: Oakland Center
cards.notes: Return to the Oakland Center food court when you need a meal; review the listed vendors and choose an option that fits your dietary needs.
cards.short_summary: A central campus meal stop with several named vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: Pioneer Food Court includes Grizzly Street Subs and Salads, Panda Express, The Halal Shack, and Slim Chickens.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required; check Dine on Campus for current menus and operating hours.

cards.title: Meet at Elliott Tower
cards.subtitle: Central campus carillon plaza
cards.notes: Use the tower plaza as a campus landmark, then listen for a scheduled live carillon performance if your weekend overlaps one.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable meeting point with a 49-bell carillon.
cards.evidence_claim: Elliott Tower has a 49-bell carillon and the university lists live Friday-at-noon performances plus special-occasion concerts.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is outdoors; concert programming varies, so consult the tower page before planning around a performance.

cards.title: Settle into Kresge Library
cards.subtitle: 100 Library Drive
cards.notes: Take a short reset in the library, then identify a study room, makerspace, or research-help option you may want during the term.
cards.short_summary: The main library combines study spaces, technology, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Kresge Library lists group and individual study rooms, a makerspace, meeting rooms, research help, and technology services.
cards.access_notes: Check the library's current hours and room-reservation rules before arrival.

cards.title: Check the OU Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: West Wilson Hall, Room 208
cards.notes: See whether an exhibition is on view, then give yourself time to walk through it; the gallery posts its regular season and hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery for contemporary and art-historical exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Art Gallery presents contemporary and art-historical exhibitions; its events are free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists regular September–May hours and says to check for upcoming exhibitions and programming.

cards.title: Look for a Meadow Brook Theatre performance
cards.subtitle: Professional theatre on the OU campus
cards.notes: Review the current production calendar and, if a show suits your schedule, plan a ticketed evening performance with friends or family.
cards.short_summary: A professional regional theatre located on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Meadow Brook Theatre is a professional regional theatre on Oakland University's campus.
cards.access_notes: Performances and ticket availability vary; check the current theatre calendar before making plans.

cards.title: Try an activity at the Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Recreation and Athletics Center, 569 Pioneer Drive
cards.notes: Bring appropriate athletic clothing, then check the facility schedule for open recreation, fitness areas, or a drop-in court activity.
cards.short_summary: A large campus recreation facility with fitness and court spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recreation Center includes an indoor track, fitness center, three-court gym, activity center, studios, and racquetball courts.
cards.access_notes: Access and open-recreation availability can vary by affiliation, reservations, classes, and facility schedule.

cards.title: Walk Grizzly Oaks Disc Golf Course
cards.subtitle: East of the Recreation and Athletics Center
cards.notes: If you have discs and daylight, start at tee 1 by the tennis courts and follow the course to its finish near the northeast corner.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus disc golf course beside the outdoor recreation complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Grizzly Oaks Disc Golf Course is east of the Recreation and Athletics Center; tee 1 is by the tennis courts and tee 18 finishes near their northeast corner.
cards.access_notes: The university says the course is open to the Oakland University community; bring your own disc and use daylight-safe conditions.

cards.title: Reserve time for Meadow Brook Hall
cards.subtitle: National Historic Landmark on the OU campus
cards.notes: Check the visitor schedule and take a tour to connect the university's founding estate with its preserved architecture, rooms, and collections.
cards.short_summary: The historic Dodge Wilson estate that helped found Oakland University.
cards.evidence_claim: Meadow Brook Hall is a National Historic Landmark on Oakland University's campus; the Wilsons donated the estate and grounds to found the university.
cards.access_notes: Tour availability is schedule-dependent; Oakland University students with valid school ID are documented as receiving free tours.

cards.title: End with a meal at Hillcrest Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Hillcrest Hall
cards.notes: Close the weekend with a campus meal and an easy chance to sit together; check the current dining schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining-hall stop designed for eating and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University identifies Hillcrest Dining Hall as a location where students can dine and socialize.
cards.access_notes: Dining access depends on a meal plan, meal swipe, or other purchase; see Dine on Campus for current hours and menus.
